# The Dust That Travels Far

## Scripture

*"For he knows how we are formed, he remembers that we are dust."* — Psalm 103:14

## Reflection

Every year, Earth passes through streams of cosmic debris left behind by ancient comets. When our atmosphere meets these particles, they streak across the sky—meteor showers. Few marvel that much of this dust is older than the sun, carried across vast distances before meeting our world.

As I watch the November meteors slip through the atmosphere, I'm mindful of this verse. God remembers we are dust. This is no insult—it's profound comfort. He remembers our frailty not to shame us but to hold us gently, the way a parent remembers a child's small, growing frame. When we feel too small, too fragile, too easily burned up by life, God reminds us that He who fashions entire galaxies from dust also tends the dust within us.

This dust isn't wasted—it returns to the earth after its journey. So too our fragile days, held in the hands of a God who knows exactly what we are made of.

*Let us rest in the tenderness with which He remembers us.*

## Prayer

Father, thank You for remembering that we are dust—fragile, yet held. When we feel small or worn away by life, remind us that the God who sculpts the stars also keeps our fragile frames. Warm our hearts with the truth that You are tender with us. Amen.
